items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (ICD dx 8/22/2025; carried in every Cardiology Clinic note as active history). Current clinic medication list (6/27/2026: levothyroxine only; prior visits tamsulosin) contains no oral anticoagulant and there is no active anticoagulant order. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension; age 71 = 1; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) and is absent. Note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure (8/2025) - bleeding risk should be weighed at review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug, is currently ordered (7/15/2026-1/7/2027) and has been continuous since 10/2/2023; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg maximum advised for QT safety in many patients. The most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 509 ms and Bazett QTc 551 ms (up from 452 ms in 2020), at or above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. No ECG has been obtained in almost three years on this drug.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 3/1/2022. The most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 581 ms and Bazett QTc 569 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Bradycardia at 58 bpm, age 95, female sex and concurrent metoprolol add further torsade risk. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are borderline-normal. No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuous amiodarone.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (5 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 381 ms, so the requirement was met on time.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the original memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025 (14 days after the start), so the monitoring requirement was met on time - although it showed QTc 555 ms, which is separately flagged for prescriber review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start precedes 3/1/2026, so the original 30-day window applies (the revised memo explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days) and the ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start) showing sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc ~435 ms, so the requirement was met on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the drug was started, and no tracing has been obtained since. The requirement is unmet and its due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the requirement was not satisfied within the required time and its due date has passed. The late tracing showed sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QTc 386 ms.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the window is still open as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the follow-up is not yet due. Given the documented long QT syndrome and potassium 5.0, the ECG should be prioritised.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing exists in the chart. That outside result could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Cardiology Clinic note of 9/1/2026 (Dr Kessler) documents INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increases warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met on time.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 3/14/2025 at the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Cardiology Clinic notes through 6/23/2026 list only famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no oral anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant order is active. Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) for secondary stroke prevention in AF; the 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a premature beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the standing order permits and the 3/1/2026 memo covers. A follow-up INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

80-year-old woman whose Cardiology Clinic notes (9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026) all carry persistent atrial fibrillation as active history. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis and no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age 80 = 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis/dysarthria 2, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1). Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried as active history in every Cardiology Clinic note (7/19/2025 - 8/4/2026); the 2/26/2025 ECG shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (166 bpm, irregularly irregular, no P waves). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive/acute systolic heart failure documented 2/26/2025, hypertension); age 48 and male sex add nothing. A score of 2 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, yet current medications are only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline and no anticoagulant order is active.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nonetheless re-listed and re-prescribed (order valid 8/20/2026-1/4/2027) with no documented reassessment of the bleed, and aspirin plus clopidogrel were continued as well. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against an explicit documented instruction to hold it pending review.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs on the current medication list. Two full-dose direct oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of 9/24/2026 (plus clopidogrel), a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.35-0.65 s, RR SD ~100 ms) with no organised P waves - at ventricular rates of 139 and 144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the tracings and the chart needs correction.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). The most recent ECG (10/8/2023, the only one since) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described that tracing as "QT acceptable", which the measured intervals do not support. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal and worth correcting; a repeat ECG on drug is also warranted.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (7/12/2026-1/9/2027) and has been continuous since 11/10/2025. The most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 547 ms and Bazett QTc 555 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. QTc had risen from 417 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related; concurrent warfarin interaction and a repeat ECG should also be addressed.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS (P axis normal, PR 178 ms), rate 81 bpm with gentle respiratory variation of RR (0.66-0.86 s) - sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. Narrow QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms, frontal axis +48 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 103 bpm with a prominent upright P before each QRS, PR 198 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms, QTc 485 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms - axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc 451 ms; the rhythm has slowed but there is no rhythm-category change, no new block and the QTc difference is under 60 ms. Earlier tracings (2/26/2025) had shown atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 468 ms (borderline prolonged, rate-related), axis +35 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.35-0.65 s (RR SD ~100 ms), no discernible P waves, therefore no measurable PR interval. Ventricular rate 144 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 449 ms, axis about -1 degree, no bundle branch block. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm, so there is no change; note that the clinic note of the same date recorded sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which these tracings contradict.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with a small low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval (PR about 158 ms); interpreted as sinus rhythm, though the P vector is leftward/superior and an ectopic atrial origin cannot be excluded. QRS 78 ms, QTc 433 ms, axis -24 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 (60 bpm, QTc 406 ms) shows the pattern of arm-lead reversal, so the limb-lead axis is not comparable; there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.
5/23/2024. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 391 ms, axis +4 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

12/25/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis +22 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.69-1.16 s (RR SD ~290 ms), no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 53 bpm. QRS 94 ms, QTc 412 ms, axis +25 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave, so this is NEW_AF. QTc essentially unchanged (404 to 412 ms).

3/9/2025. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, PR 108 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 414 ms, axis +60 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Nearly identical to the prior tracing of 3/8/2025 (62 bpm, QTc 445 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc difference under 60 ms. Note this remains the most recent tracing despite a documented long QT syndrome and a new haloperidol order.
8/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 407 ms, axis +52 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc 460 ms, axis +64 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 2/2/2020 was also sinus (74 bpm) but with flat/inverted T waves and a longer QT, QTc about 521 ms; the QTc has fallen by roughly 60 ms, recorded as QTC_DECREASE_60. No rhythm or block change.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR essentially fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms, axis +53 degrees, no conduction block. Versus the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QTc 412 ms) there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a conducted P before every QRS but a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QTc 383 ms, frontal axis +5 degrees. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 was sinus 51 bpm with PR 186 ms and QTc 365 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no listed change category (rhythm unchanged, no bundle branch block, QTc change well under 60 ms).

9/13/2025 07:17. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: chaotic irregularly irregular RR 0.29-0.58 s, no P waves, no measurable PR; mean ventricular rate 153 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis -20 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a discrete P wave and a single premature beat, so this is NEW_AF. QTc change (420 to 426 ms) is not significant.

11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 396 ms, axis +13 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block - matching the same-day clinic note. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 was sinus 67 bpm with a much longer QT (QTc about 538 ms); repolarisation has normalised, a fall of roughly 140 ms, recorded as QTC_DECREASE_60.

2/15/2025. Technically noisy tracing with muscle/motion artefact in the first and last thirds; the clean segments show a regular rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.80-0.82 s) with an upright P before each QRS, PR 176 ms - sinus rhythm. Artefact spikes cause spurious short intervals and should not be read as tachyarrhythmia. QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR fixed at 0.54 s with one upright P per QRS (PR 160 ms) - not atrial flutter, there is a single atrial deflection per cycle. QRS 96 ms, QTc 398 ms, axis +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 was also sinus tachycardia (115 bpm, QTc 395 ms): no rhythm, block or QTc change. Despite the atrial flutter history, no flutter is present on this tracing.

3/14/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm (RR 0.96-1.00 s) with one interpolated premature beat and a compensatory pause; a consistent upright P precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 200 ms. QRS 98 ms, QTc 407 ms, frontal axis about -33 degrees (left axis deviation; lead II net negative). No bundle branch block. This tracing is in sinus rhythm and does not exclude the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded the same day. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

4/29/2026. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 386 ms, no AV or bundle branch block. The limb leads show globally negative complexes in I and II with preserved normal precordial R-wave progression, giving a computed frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme/north-west quadrant); this pattern is typical of left/right arm electrode reversal and the axis should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

11/10/2023. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a low flat T wave: QT 509 ms, Bazett QTc 551 ms. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 452 ms, so QTc has risen by roughly 100 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. On citalopram 40 mg daily; flagged for prescriber review.

3/8/2026. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis +57 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The T wave is inverted in I, aVL and V2-V3 and upright in III/aVR with QT about 408 ms, QTc 435 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. Some leads show late low-amplitude baseline drift that must not be mistaken for a very long T wave. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison; it satisfies the 30-day post-escitalopram requirement.

1/13/2019. Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 370 ms, axis -4 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Prior tracing 12/13/2018 was sinus 66 bpm with PR 198 ms, QRS 106 ms and QTc 393 ms: no rhythm change, no bundle branch block on either, and QTc difference well under 60 ms.

10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation abnormality: the T wave is broad and late-peaking, QT 498 ms giving Bazett QTc 531 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 170 ms, a QTC_INCREASE_60. This is the most recent ECG on file and the patient remains on escitalopram, so it is flagged for prescriber review.

7/13/2022. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 0.40-0.46 s, RR SD 12 ms) with a discrete low-amplitude atrial wave preceding each QRS at a fixed PR of about 144 ms and only one atrial deflection per cycle - read as sinus tachycardia rather than atrial fibrillation or 2:1 flutter, although the P morphology is atypical. QRS 82 ms, QTc 419 ms, axis about 0 degrees, no bundle branch block and no pacing artefact despite the pacemaker history. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 was atrial fibrillation (RR 0.38-0.83 s, no P waves), so RESOLVED_AF. QTc change (441 to 419 ms) is not significant.
5/12/2025. Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 102 ms (no bundle branch block), QTc 444 ms, axis +34 degrees. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

7/16/2022. Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with a broad P wave and PR about 200 ms - at the upper limit but not clearly beyond it, so no first-degree AV block is coded. QRS 78 ms, QTc 411 ms, axis -15 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 5/16/2021 was sinus 87 bpm with QTc 398 ms: no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

7/17/2024. Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with a conducted but delayed P wave, PR about 220 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS is widened to 132 ms with a broad monophasic negative complex in V1-V2, absent septal q and a broad R in I and V6, i.e. left bundle branch block. QTc 454 ms, frontal axis -21 degrees. The prior tracing of 6/3/2024 showed the same LBBB with QRS 132 ms, PR 212 ms and QTc 452 ms, so there is no new or resolved bundle branch block and no significant QTc change.

3/19/2025. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 435 ms, axis +45 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Virtually identical to the prior tracing of 3/18/2025 (102 bpm, QTc 431 ms): no rhythm, block or QTc change.
9/22/2025. Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 391 ms, axis -21 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm/bradycardia at 58 bpm with an upright P before each QRS, PR 196 ms. QRS 88 ms, axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block. Very prolonged repolarisation with a broad late T wave: QT about 581 ms, Bazett QTc 569 ms. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 was atrial fibrillation at 128 bpm (RR 0.2-0.9 s, no P waves) with QTc about 435 ms, so this tracing shows RESOLVED_AF together with a QTC_INCREASE_60 of roughly 130 ms. On chronic amiodarone; flagged for prescriber review.

5/1/2022. Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, PR 170 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 434 ms, axis +51 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Prior tracing 7/27/2019 was sinus 75 bpm with QTc 431 ms: no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before every QRS, PR 126 ms. QRS 90 ms, QTc 427 ms, axis +66 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 421 ms, axis +58 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (100 bpm, QTc 417 ms); no rhythm, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a regular upright P before each QRS, PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms with tall left precordial voltage, QTc 405 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. Prior tracing 5/22/2023 was sinus 57 bpm with one premature beat, QTc 380 ms - no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more. Despite the AF history this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS now narrow at 102 ms, QTc 428 ms, frontal axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 166 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; that pattern has disappeared, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 479 to 428 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Grossly prolonged repolarisation: QT 547 ms, Bazett QTc 555 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025 (sinus/bradycardic 47 bpm with ectopy, QTc 417 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; QTc has increased by about 140 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Flagged separately for prescriber review on a QT watch-list drug.

9/17/2024. Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.41-1.07 s, RR SD ~190 ms) with no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, so no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 102 bpm. QRS 80 ms, QTc 413 ms, frontal axis about -48 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. Corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 9/16/2024. Only ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs on the current medication list. The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (7/12/2026-1/9/2027) and has been continuous since 11/10/2025. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against an explicit documented instruction to hold it pending review.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs on the current medication list. The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.35-0.65 s, RR SD ~100 ms) with no organised P waves - at ventricular rates of 139 and 144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the tracings and the chart needs correction.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described that tracing as "QT acceptable", which the measured intervals do not support. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal and worth correcting; a repeat ECG on drug is also warranted.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (7/12/2026-1/9/2027) and has been continuous since 11/10/2025. The most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 547 ms and Bazett QTc 555 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. QTc had risen from 417 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started. arguments.explanation: 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS now narrow at 102 ms, QTc 428 ms, frontal axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 166 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; that pattern has disappeared, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 479 to 428 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nonetheless re-listed and re-prescribed (order valid 8/20/2026-1/4/2027) with no documented reassessment of the bleed, and aspirin plus clopidogrel were continued as well. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against an explicit documented instruction to hold it pending review.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs on the current medication list. Two full-dose direct oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of 9/24/2026 (plus clopidogrel), a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.35-0.65 s, RR SD ~100 ms) with no organised P waves - at ventricular rates of 139 and 144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the tracings and the chart needs correction.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). The most recent ECG (10/8/2023, the only one since) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described that tracing as "QT acceptable", which the measured intervals do not support. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal and worth correcting; a repeat ECG on drug is also warranted.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (7/12/2026-1/9/2027) and has been continuous since 11/10/2025. The most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 547 ms and Bazett QTc 555 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. QTc had risen from 417 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related; concurrent warfarin interaction and a repeat ECG should also be addressed.

Nguyen, PharmD documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the standing order permits and the 3/1/2026 memo covers. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension; age 71 = 1; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) and is absent. Note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure (8/2025) - bleeding risk should be weighed at review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug, is currently ordered (7/15/2026-1/7/2027) and has been continuous since 10/2/2023; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg maximum advised for QT safety in many patients. The most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 509 ms and Bazett QTc 551 ms (up from 452 ms in 2020), at or above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. No ECG has been obtained in almost three years on this drug.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 3/1/2022. The most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 581 ms and Bazett QTc 569 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Bradycardia at 58 bpm, age 95, female sex and concurrent metoprolol add further torsade risk. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are borderline-normal. No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuous amiodarone.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (5 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 381 ms, so the requirement was met on time.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the original memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025 (14 days after the start), so the monitoring requirement was met on time - although it showed QTc 555 ms, which is separately flagged for prescriber review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start precedes 3/1/2026, so the original 30-day window applies (the revised memo explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days) and the ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start) showing sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc ~435 ms, so the requirement was met on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the drug was started, and no tracing has been obtained since. The requirement is unmet and its due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the requirement was not satisfied within the required time and its due date has passed. The late tracing showed sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QTc 386 ms.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the window is still open as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the follow-up is not yet due. Given the documented long QT syndrome and potassium 5.0, the ECG should be prioritised.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing exists in the chart. That outside result could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Cardiology Clinic note of 9/1/2026 (Dr Kessler) documents INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increases warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met on time.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 3/14/2025 at the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Cardiology Clinic notes through 6/23/2026 list only famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no oral anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant order is active. Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) for secondary stroke prevention in AF; the 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a premature beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the standing order permits and the 3/1/2026 memo covers. A follow-up INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

80-year-old woman whose Cardiology Clinic notes (9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026) all carry persistent atrial fibrillation as active history. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis and no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age 80 = 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis/dysarthria 2, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1). Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried as active history in every Cardiology Clinic note (7/19/2025 - 8/4/2026); the 2/26/2025 ECG shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (166 bpm, irregularly irregular, no P waves). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive/acute systolic heart failure documented 2/26/2025, hypertension); age 48 and male sex add nothing. A score of 2 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, yet current medications are only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline and no anticoagulant order is active.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nonetheless re-listed and re-prescribed (order valid 8/20/2026-1/4/2027) with no documented reassessment of the bleed, and aspirin plus clopidogrel were continued as well. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against an explicit documented instruction to hold it pending review.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs on the current medication list. Two full-dose direct oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of 9/24/2026 (plus clopidogrel), a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.35-0.65 s, RR SD ~100 ms) with no organised P waves - at ventricular rates of 139 and 144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the tracings and the chart needs correction.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). The most recent ECG (10/8/2023, the only one since) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described that tracing as "QT acceptable", which the measured intervals do not support. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal and worth correcting; a repeat ECG on drug is also warranted.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (7/12/2026-1/9/2027) and has been continuous since 11/10/2025. The most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 547 ms and Bazett QTc 555 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. QTc had risen from 417 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related; concurrent warfarin interaction and a repeat ECG should also be addressed.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS (P axis normal, PR 178 ms), rate 81 bpm with gentle respiratory variation of RR (0.66-0.86 s) - sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. Narrow QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms, frontal axis +48 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 103 bpm with a prominent upright P before each QRS, PR 198 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms, QTc 485 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms - axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc 451 ms; the rhythm has slowed but there is no rhythm-category change, no new block and the QTc difference is under 60 ms. Earlier tracings (2/26/2025) had shown atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 468 ms (borderline prolonged, rate-related), axis +35 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.35-0.65 s (RR SD ~100 ms), no discernible P waves, therefore no measurable PR interval. Ventricular rate 144 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 449 ms, axis about -1 degree, no bundle branch block. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm, so there is no change; note that the clinic note of the same date recorded sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which these tracings contradict.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with a small low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval (PR about 158 ms); interpreted as sinus rhythm, though the P vector is leftward/superior and an ectopic atrial origin cannot be excluded. QRS 78 ms, QTc 433 ms, axis -24 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 (60 bpm, QTc 406 ms) shows the pattern of arm-lead reversal, so the limb-lead axis is not comparable; there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.
5/23/2024. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 391 ms, axis +4 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

12/25/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis +22 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR essentially fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms, axis +53 degrees, no conduction block. Versus the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QTc 412 ms) there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation abnormality: the T wave is broad and late-peaking, QT 498 ms giving Bazett QTc 531 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 170 ms, a QTC_INCREASE_60. This is the most recent ECG on file and the patient remains on escitalopram, so it is flagged for prescriber review.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before every QRS, PR 126 ms. QRS 90 ms, QTc 427 ms, axis +66 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 421 ms, axis +58 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (100 bpm, QTc 417 ms); no rhythm, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a regular upright P before each QRS, PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms with tall left precordial voltage, QTc 405 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. Prior tracing 5/22/2023 was sinus 57 bpm with one premature beat, QTc 380 ms - no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more. Despite the AF history this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS now narrow at 102 ms, QTc 428 ms, frontal axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 166 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; that pattern has disappeared, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 479 to 428 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Grossly prolonged repolarisation: QT 547 ms, Bazett QTc 555 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025 (sinus/bradycardic 47 bpm with ectopy, QTc 417 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; QTc has increased by about 140 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Flagged separately for prescriber review on a QT watch-list drug.

9/17/2024. Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.41-1.07 s, RR SD ~190 ms) with no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, so no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 102 bpm. QRS 80 ms, QTc 413 ms, frontal axis about -48 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. Corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 9/16/2024. Only ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

arguments.explanation: 11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.69-1.16 s (RR SD ~290 ms), no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 53 bpm. QRS 94 ms, QTc 412 ms, axis +25 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave, so this is NEW_AF. QTc essentially unchanged (404 to 412 ms).

Regular P wave before every QRS (P axis normal, PR 178 ms), rate 81 bpm with gentle respiratory variation of RR (0.66-0.86 s) - sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. Narrow QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms, frontal axis +48 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 103 bpm with a prominent upright P before each QRS, PR 198 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms, QTc 485 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms - axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc 451 ms; the rhythm has slowed but there is no rhythm-category change, no new block and the QTc difference is under 60 ms. Earlier tracings (2/26/2025) had shown atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 468 ms (borderline prolonged, rate-related), axis +35 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.35-0.65 s (RR SD ~100 ms), no discernible P waves, therefore no measurable PR interval. Ventricular rate 144 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 449 ms, axis about -1 degree, no bundle branch block. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm, so there is no change; note that the clinic note of the same date recorded sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which these tracings contradict.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with a small low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval (PR about 158 ms); interpreted as sinus rhythm, though the P vector is leftward/superior and an ectopic atrial origin cannot be excluded. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 (60 bpm, QTc 406 ms) shows the pattern of arm-lead reversal, so the limb-lead axis is not comparable; there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.
5/23/2024. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 391 ms, axis +4 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

12/25/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis +22 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.69-1.16 s (RR SD ~290 ms), no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 53 bpm. QRS 94 ms, QTc 412 ms, axis +25 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave, so this is NEW_AF. QTc essentially unchanged (404 to 412 ms).

3/9/2025. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, PR 108 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 414 ms, axis +60 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Nearly identical to the prior tracing of 3/8/2025 (62 bpm, QTc 445 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc difference under 60 ms. Note this remains the most recent tracing despite a documented long QT syndrome and a new haloperidol order.
8/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 407 ms, axis +52 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc 460 ms, axis +64 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. No rhythm or block change.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR essentially fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms, axis +53 degrees, no conduction block. QTc change (420 to 426 ms) is not significant.

Technically noisy tracing with muscle/motion artefact in the first and last thirds; the clean segments show a regular rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.80-0.82 s) with an upright P before each QRS, PR 176 ms - sinus rhythm. Despite the atrial flutter history, no flutter is present on this tracing.

This is the most recent ECG on file and the patient remains on escitalopram, so it is flagged for prescriber review.

QTc fell from 479 to 428 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Grossly prolonged repolarisation: QT 547 ms, Bazett QTc 555 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025 (sinus/bradycardic 47 bpm with ectopy, QTc 417 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; QTc has increased by about 140 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Flagged separately for prescriber review on a QT watch-list drug.

9/17/2024. Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.41-1.07 s, RR SD ~190 ms) with no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, so no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 102 bpm. QRS 80 ms, QTc 413 ms, frontal axis about -48 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. Corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 9/16/2024. Only ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

arguments.explanation: 3/14/2025. No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuous amiodarone.

Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the tracings and the chart needs correction.

The most recent ECG (10/8/2023, the only one since) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 547 ms and Bazett QTc 555 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. QTc had risen from 417 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related; concurrent warfarin interaction and a repeat ECG should also be addressed.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS (P axis normal, PR 178 ms), rate 81 bpm with gentle respiratory variation of RR (0.66-0.86 s) - sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. Narrow QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms, frontal axis +48 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 103 bpm with a prominent upright P before each QRS, PR 198 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms, QTc 485 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms - axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc 451 ms; the rhythm has slowed but there is no rhythm-category change, no new block and the QTc difference is under 60 ms. Earlier tracings (2/26/2025) had shown atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 468 ms (borderline prolonged, rate-related), axis +35 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.35-0.65 s (RR SD ~100 ms), no discernible P waves, therefore no measurable PR interval. Ventricular rate 144 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 449 ms, axis about -1 degree, no bundle branch block. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm, so there is no change; note that the clinic note of the same date recorded sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which these tracings contradict.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with a small low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval (PR about 158 ms); interpreted as sinus rhythm, though the P vector is leftward/superior and an ectopic atrial origin cannot be excluded. QRS 78 ms, QTc 433 ms, axis -24 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 (60 bpm, QTc 406 ms) shows the pattern of arm-lead reversal, so the limb-lead axis is not comparable; there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.
5/23/2024. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 391 ms, axis +4 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

12/25/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis +22 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.69-1.16 s (RR SD ~290 ms), no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 53 bpm. QRS 94 ms, QTc 412 ms, axis +25 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave, so this is NEW_AF. QTc essentially unchanged (404 to 412 ms).

3/9/2025. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, PR 108 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 414 ms, axis +60 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Nearly identical to the prior tracing of 3/8/2025 (62 bpm, QTc 445 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc difference under 60 ms. Note this remains the most recent tracing despite a documented long QT syndrome and a new haloperidol order.
8/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 407 ms, axis +52 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc 460 ms, axis +64 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 2/2/2020 was also sinus (74 bpm) but with flat/inverted T waves and a longer QT, QTc about 521 ms; the QTc has fallen by roughly 60 ms, recorded as QTC_DECREASE_60. No rhythm or block change.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR essentially fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms, axis +53 degrees, no conduction block. Versus the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QTc 412 ms) there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a conducted P before every QRS but a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QTc 383 ms, frontal axis +5 degrees. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 was sinus 51 bpm with PR 186 ms and QTc 365 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no listed change category (rhythm unchanged, no bundle branch block, QTc change well under 60 ms).

9/13/2025 07:17. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: chaotic irregularly irregular RR 0.29-0.58 s, no P waves, no measurable PR; mean ventricular rate 153 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis -20 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a discrete P wave and a single premature beat, so this is NEW_AF. QTc change (420 to 426 ms) is not significant.

11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 396 ms, axis +13 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block - matching the same-day clinic note. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 was sinus 67 bpm with a much longer QT (QTc about 538 ms); repolarisation has normalised, a fall of roughly 140 ms, recorded as QTC_DECREASE_60.

2/15/2025. Technically noisy tracing with muscle/motion artefact in the first and last thirds; the clean segments show a regular rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.80-0.82 s) with an upright P before each QRS, PR 176 ms - sinus rhythm. Artefact spikes cause spurious short intervals and should not be read as tachyarrhythmia. QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR fixed at 0.54 s with one upright P per QRS (PR 160 ms) - not atrial flutter, there is a single atrial deflection per cycle. QRS 96 ms, QTc 398 ms, axis +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 was also sinus tachycardia (115 bpm, QTc 395 ms): no rhythm, block or QTc change. Despite the atrial flutter history, no flutter is present on this tracing.

3/14/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm (RR 0.96-1.00 s) with one interpolated premature beat and a compensatory pause; a consistent upright P precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 200 ms. QRS 98 ms, QTc 407 ms, frontal axis about -33 degrees (left axis deviation; lead II net negative). No bundle branch block. This tracing is in sinus rhythm and does not exclude the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded the same day. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation abnormality: the T wave is broad and late-peaking, QT 498 ms giving Bazett QTc 531 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 170 ms, a QTC_INCREASE_60. This is the most recent ECG on file and the patient remains on escitalopram, so it is flagged for prescriber review.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before every QRS, PR 126 ms. QRS 90 ms, QTc 427 ms, axis +66 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 421 ms, axis +58 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (100 bpm, QTc 417 ms); no rhythm, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a regular upright P before each QRS, PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms with tall left precordial voltage, QTc 405 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. Prior tracing 5/22/2023 was sinus 57 bpm with one premature beat, QTc 380 ms - no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more. Despite the AF history this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS now narrow at 102 ms, QTc 428 ms, frontal axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 166 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; that pattern has disappeared, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 479 to 428 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Grossly prolonged repolarisation: QT 547 ms, Bazett QTc 555 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025 (sinus/bradycardic 47 bpm with ectopy, QTc 417 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; QTc has increased by about 140 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Flagged separately for prescriber review on a QT watch-list drug.

9/17/2024. Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.41-1.07 s, RR SD ~190 ms) with no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, so no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 102 bpm. QRS 80 ms, QTc 413 ms, frontal axis about -48 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. Corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 9/16/2024. Only ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 3/14/2025 at the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Cardiology Clinic notes through 6/23/2026 list only famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no oral anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant order is active. Anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) for secondary stroke prevention in AF; the 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a premature beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the standing order permits and the 3/1/2026 memo covers. A follow-up INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

80-year-old woman whose Cardiology Clinic notes (9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026) all carry persistent atrial fibrillation as active history. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis and no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age 80 = 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis/dysarthria 2, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1). Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried as active history in every Cardiology Clinic note (7/19/2025 - 8/4/2026); the 2/26/2025 ECG shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (166 bpm, irregularly irregular, no P waves). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive/acute systolic heart failure documented 2/26/2025, hypertension); age 48 and male sex add nothing. A score of 2 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, yet current medications are only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline and no anticoagulant order is active.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nonetheless re-listed and re-prescribed (order valid 8/20/2026-1/4/2027) with no documented reassessment of the bleed, and aspirin plus clopidogrel were continued as well. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against an explicit documented instruction to hold it pending review.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs on the current medication list. Two full-dose direct oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active as of 9/24/2026 (plus clopidogrel), a major bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.35-0.65 s, RR SD ~100 ms) with no organised P waves - at ventricular rates of 139 and 144 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the tracings and the chart needs correction.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). The most recent ECG (10/8/2023, the only one since) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 498 ms and Bazett QTc 531 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described that tracing as "QT acceptable", which the measured intervals do not support. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal and worth correcting; a repeat ECG on drug is also warranted.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (7/12/2026-1/9/2027) and has been continuous since 11/10/2025. The most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 547 ms and Bazett QTc 555 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. QTc had risen from 417 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related; concurrent warfarin interaction and a repeat ECG should also be addressed.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS (P axis normal, PR 178 ms), rate 81 bpm with gentle respiratory variation of RR (0.66-0.86 s) - sinus rhythm, confirming the same-day clinic note. Narrow QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms, frontal axis +48 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 103 bpm with a prominent upright P before each QRS, PR 198 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms, QTc 485 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms - axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc 451 ms; the rhythm has slowed but there is no rhythm-category change, no new block and the QTc difference is under 60 ms. Earlier tracings (2/26/2025) had shown atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

5/21/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 468 ms (borderline prolonged, rate-related), axis +35 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.35-0.65 s (RR SD ~100 ms), no discernible P waves, therefore no measurable PR interval. Ventricular rate 144 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 449 ms, axis about -1 degree, no bundle branch block. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm, so there is no change; note that the clinic note of the same date recorded sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which these tracings contradict.

8/2/2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with a small low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval (PR about 158 ms); interpreted as sinus rhythm, though the P vector is leftward/superior and an ectopic atrial origin cannot be excluded. QRS 78 ms, QTc 433 ms, axis -24 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 (60 bpm, QTc 406 ms) shows the pattern of arm-lead reversal, so the limb-lead axis is not comparable; there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.
5/23/2024. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc 391 ms, axis +4 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

12/25/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis +22 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR 0.69-1.16 s (RR SD ~290 ms), no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval; mean ventricular rate 53 bpm. QRS 94 ms, QTc 412 ms, axis +25 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave, so this is NEW_AF. QTc essentially unchanged (404 to 412 ms).

3/9/2025. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, PR 108 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 414 ms, axis +60 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Nearly identical to the prior tracing of 3/8/2025 (62 bpm, QTc 445 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc difference under 60 ms. Note this remains the most recent tracing despite a documented long QT syndrome and a new haloperidol order.
8/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 407 ms, axis +52 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc 460 ms, axis +64 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 2/2/2020 was also sinus (74 bpm) but with flat/inverted T waves and a longer QT, QTc about 521 ms; the QTc has fallen by roughly 60 ms, recorded as QTC_DECREASE_60. No rhythm or block change.

1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR essentially fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 94 ms, QTc 394 ms, axis +53 degrees, no conduction block. Versus the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QTc 412 ms) there is no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a conducted P before every QRS but a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QTc 383 ms, frontal axis +5 degrees. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 was sinus 51 bpm with PR 186 ms and QTc 365 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no listed change category (rhythm unchanged, no bundle branch block, QTc change well under 60 ms).

9/13/2025 07:17. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: chaotic irregularly irregular RR 0.29-0.58 s, no P waves, no measurable PR; mean ventricular rate 153 bpm. QRS 98 ms, QTc 426 ms, axis -20 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a discrete P wave and a single premature beat, so this is NEW_AF. QTc change (420 to 426 ms) is not significant.

11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 396 ms, axis +13 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block - matching the same-day clinic note. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 was sinus 67 bpm with a much longer QT (QTc about 538 ms); repolarisation has normalised, a fall of roughly 140 ms, recorded as QTC_DECREASE_60.

2/15/2025. Technically noisy tracing with muscle/motion artefact in the first and last thirds; the clean segments show a regular rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.80-0.82 s) with an upright P before each QRS, PR 176 ms - sinus rhythm. Artefact spikes cause spurious short intervals and should not be read as tachyarrhythmia. QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

6/26/2023. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR fixed at 0.54 s with one upright P per QRS (PR 160 ms) - not atrial flutter, there is a single atrial deflection per cycle. QRS 96 ms, QTc 398 ms, axis +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 7/4/2022 was also sinus tachycardia (115 bpm, QTc 395 ms): no rhythm, block or QTc change. Despite the atrial flutter history, no flutter is present on this tracing.

3/14/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm (RR 0.96-1.00 s) with one interpolated premature beat and a compensatory pause; a consistent upright P precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 200 ms. QRS 98 ms, QTc 407 ms, frontal axis about -33 degrees (left axis deviation; lead II net negative). No bundle branch block. This tracing is in sinus rhythm and does not exclude the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded the same day. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

4/29/2026. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 386 ms, no AV or bundle branch block. The limb leads show globally negative complexes in I and II with preserved normal precordial R-wave progression, giving a computed frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme/north-west quadrant); this pattern is typical of left/right arm electrode reversal and the axis should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

11/10/2023. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a low flat T wave: QT 509 ms, Bazett QTc 551 ms. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 452 ms, so QTc has risen by roughly 100 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. On citalopram 40 mg daily; flagged for prescriber review.

10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation abnormality: the T wave is broad and late-peaking, QT 498 ms giving Bazett QTc 531 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 170 ms, a QTC_INCREASE_60. This is the most recent ECG on file and the patient remains on escitalopram, so it is flagged for prescriber review.

4/19/2024. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR fixed at 0.50 s with an upright P before every QRS, PR 126 ms. QRS 90 ms, QTc 427 ms, axis +66 degrees, no AV or bundle branch block. Single ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 421 ms, axis +58 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (100 bpm, QTc 417 ms); no rhythm, block or QTc change.

10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a regular upright P before each QRS, PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms with tall left precordial voltage, QTc 405 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. Prior tracing 5/22/2023 was sinus 57 bpm with one premature beat, QTc 380 ms - no rhythm, block or QTc change of 60 ms or more. Despite the AF history this tracing is in sinus rhythm.

12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS now narrow at 102 ms, QTc 428 ms, frontal axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed a markedly widened QRS of 166 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block; that pattern has disappeared, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from 479 to 428 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Grossly prolonged repolarisation: QT 547 ms, Bazett QTc 555 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025 (sinus/bradycardic 47 bpm with ectopy, QTc 417 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; QTc has increased by about 140 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Flagged separately for prescriber review on a QT watch-list drug.

9/17/2024. Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.41-1.07 s, RR SD ~190 ms) with no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, so no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate 102 bpm. QRS 80 ms, QTc 413 ms, frontal axis about -48 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. Corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 9/16/2024. Only ECG on file, no prior for comparison.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (ICD dx 8/22/2025; carried in every Cardiology Clinic note as active history). Current clinic medication list (6/27/2026: levothyroxine only; prior visits tamsulosin) contains no oral anticoagulant and there is no active anticoagulant order. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension; age 71 = 1; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1) and is absent. Note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure (8/2025) - bleeding risk should be weighed at review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug, is currently ordered (7/15/2026-1/7/2027) and has been continuous since 10/2/2023; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg maximum advised for QT safety in many patients. The most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 509 ms and Bazett QTc 551 ms (up from 452 ms in 2020), at or above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. No ECG has been obtained in almost three years on this drug.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is currently ordered (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 3/1/2022. The most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 581 ms and Bazett QTc 569 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Bradycardia at 58 bpm, age 95, female sex and concurrent metoprolol add further torsade risk. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are borderline-normal. No ECG has been obtained since 2022 despite continuous amiodarone.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (5 days after the start) and showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 381 ms, so the requirement was met on time.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the original memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025 (14 days after the start), so the monitoring requirement was met on time - although it showed QTc 555 ms, which is separately flagged for prescriber review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start precedes 3/1/2026, so the original 30-day window applies (the revised memo explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days) and the ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start) showing sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc ~435 ms, so the requirement was met on time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the drug was started, and no tracing has been obtained since. The requirement is unmet and its due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the requirement was not satisfied within the required time and its due date has passed. The late tracing showed sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QTc 386 ms.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the window is still open as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the follow-up is not yet due. Given the documented long QT syndrome and potassium 5.0, the ECG should be prioritised.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing exists in the chart. That outside result could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.
